text_overlays.text: NBA teams that got bought for INSANE AMOUNTS OF MONEY!

A private recording of Los Angeles Clippers owner, Donald Sterling, making racist comments got leaked online, so the NBA banned him from the league for life and told him he had to sell his team. But the price that team ended up selling for is the part that stunned everyone. His wife handled the sale, and a former Microsoft CEO named Steve Ballmer won the bidding at two billion dollars, which shattered the record. Just weeks earlier the Milwaukee Bucks had sold for 550 million, and Sterling himself bought the Clippers back in 1981 for around twelve and a half million dollars, yet Ballmer even outbid a group that included Oprah Winfrey. To almost everyone watching this looked insane, because Forbes said the team only made about fifteen million dollars in profit the year before, so paying two billion felt like lighting money on fire. But Ballmer wasn't paying that number for the reason you'd expect. He had already tried and failed to buy the Seattle SuperSonics and the Sacramento Kings, and he was tired of losing, so he wanted a team so badly that he promised himself he would never get outbid again, no matter the price. But the people calling him crazy forgot one thing. The team he supposedly overpaid for is now worth around seven and a half billion dollars, because the purchase everyone laughed at instantly reset the value of every franchise in the league.
